question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ we will set our result equal to $4.$ 

From the equation $y=(x-5k)(x+7k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=5k$ and ${x}_{2}=-7k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{5k+(-7k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2k}{2} \\  & =-k\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-k & =4 \\ k & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
